system_description.narrative_title: Fractured Multipolar Order: War, Energy Shocks, AI, Migration & Monetary Stress
system_description.narrative_summary: The global geopolitical order is an open, tightly coupled system under stress from overlapping regional wars, energy and maritime disruption, accelerated AI-driven economic realignment, and acute monetary and supply-chain volatility. State and non-state actors, major corporations and financial authorities dynamically interact across contested sea lanes, markets and digital domains, producing cascading risks—from refugee surges to spikes in commodity and borrowing costs. Short-term crisis management (military strikes, currency intervention, ad hoc coalitions) competes with longer-term structural shifts (tech concentration, deglobalizing supply chains, climate-driven resource constraints).
system_description.scope: Nation-states and regional blocs; major corporations in energy, technology and finance; security alliances and military operations; maritime trade routes and chokepoints; global commodity markets (oil, LNG, food); monetary authorities and bond/FX markets; supply chains, data centers and AI industrial investments; migration flows and climate-related resource stress.
system_description.super_system: Planetary socio-economic-environmental system (globalized civilization, biosphere and international political economy)

variables.name: US–Iran confrontation
variables.description: The United States and Iran, together with their regional proxies and Gulf partners, are locked in a widening military and diplomatic confrontation marked by escalating strikes and shifting regional alignments.

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine war
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine, backed by Western military and economic support, are engaged in a protracted war that is evolving toward targeted strikes on critical infrastructure and adaptive Ukrainian tactics.

variables.name: China–US tech and economic rivalry
variables.description: China and the United States, along with allied democracies, are contesting technological and economic leadership across AI, semiconductors and critical supply chains, driving export controls, subsidies and strategic decoupling.

variables.name: Energy markets and maritime chokepoints
variables.description: Gulf producers, shipping intermediaries and global oil firms are reconfiguring trade and pricing as attacks, tanker rerouting and new security coalitions threaten chokepoints such as the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea.

variables.name: Global monetary policy and currency dynamics
variables.description: Major central banks (the US Federal Reserve, BOJ, ECB and others), markets and treasuries are grappling with diverging rate paths, bond-market stress and episodes of coordinated or unilateral currency intervention that are reshaping capital flows and policy credibility.
